label: dense memory: sequence contains v / k / e / 3 (peak on 0 after leading v)
explanation: Dense, graded feature (active on ~40% of all steps). It acts as a persistent memory that one of the tokens v, k, e or 3 has appeared earlier in the sequence, with v strongest (rate is 1.0 whenever v is the token being output; first_tok=v gives 1.6x lift). Once such a token is seen, the feature stays on through the rest of the original phase, the delimiter and the copy phase. It is not tied to position, L, phase, or copy correctness. Magnitude is largest when the sequence starts with v (especially v v) and the current input is the digit 0, where it reaches the max of about 7. Activations on later original tokens and on <DEL> are about 0.6-0.8 of max, and the feature decays during the copy phase after v is output. The predicate seen([v,k,e,3]) captures about 82% of activation mass on dev but has only about 0.56 precision against a 0.40 base rate. Widening the set (q,u,c,t,w) pushes mass recall to 0.92 at lower precision, consistent with a graded token-weighted memory rather than a crisp set. Low-level firing (bottom quartiles, ~0.1-0.4) is diffuse and appears in sequences without these tokens.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: v, k, 3, e; input phase: 0, i, 2, r; delimiter step: ) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: v, k, e, 3; delimiter step: v, k, e, 3; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, L=3 & t=4, L=9 & t=11.
